title: Bitcoin (BTC) Falls as $550 Million in Risky Crypto Bets Wiped Out
summary: Cryptocurrencies fell on Wednesday as a wave of forced selling swept across digital-asset venues, with broader market jitters further weighing on risk appetite.

title: San Francisco Passes Data Center Moratorium in Hometown of AI
summary: San Francisco, home to some of the world’s most valuable artificial-intelligence companies, is temporarily banning new data centers within its borders.

title: Alibaba’s Joe Tsai Says Open Source Is Europe’s Best Shot at AI
summary: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. Chairman Joe Tsai said open-source artificial intelligence is Europe’s best route to technological independence from the US and China, and urged the region to build out its own computing infrastructure to train and run AI models.

title: National Compute Takes On AI Gatekeepers
summary: America’s AI edge depends on who controls compute.  Anjney Midha, the CEO of National Compute, joined Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about his plans to turn AI infrastructure into a shared national grid, opening powerful chips to students, researchers, and startups across the country. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Apollo’s Push for Private Credit Transparency
summary: Apollo is pushing to make private credit more transparent and easier to trade. The firm has now traded more than $35 billion of private credit and is putting daily valuations on an $850 billion portfolio. John Cortese, Co-Head of Corporate Credit at Apollo Asset Management, discusses the effort on Bloomberg Open Interest. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: AI Agent Adoption Soars on Consumer, Search Trends
summary:
Meta's Muse has topped 6.6 million downloads since its Sept. 8 launch and reached 1.8 million daily active users, as consumers show they're ready to hand over their personal information for a chance at some AI assistance.  
Seema Shah, VP: Insights at Sensor Tower, discusses the growth of personal AI agents, Zuckerberg's Muse, and the broader AI market. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: SpaceX Reported to Be in $40 Billion Nvidia Chip-Financing Talks
summary: Elon Musk's SpaceX is in talks with banks and investors to raise $40 billion to buy chips from Nvidia. Sarah Frier has more on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Google, Unity Launch Platform to Create Video Games From Prompts
summary: Alphabet Inc.’s Google and gaming tools developer Unity Software Inc. announced a new platform that will allow people to create video games from simple text prompts, marking the latest incursion of generative artificial intelligence into artistic and creative industries.

title: Video-Game Designer Behind ‘Sky,’ ‘Journey’ Raises $35 Million
summary: A studio led by the makers of the hit titles Sky: Children of the Light and Journey has raised $35 million in new funding to upend the viral “friendslop” genre of casual, whimsical video games played socially online.

title: Apollo’s Wassenaar Sees Underinvestment Risk in Infrastructure (Correct)
summary: Olivia Wassenaar, Apollo's global head of infrastructure, says the firm deployed more than $20 billion in infrastructure originations in the third quarter, partnering with investment-grade companies and investing in areas including gas processing. Speaking on "Bloomberg Surveillance," Wassenaar also says the opportunity extends beyond AI data centers to the power supply, electrical grid, natural-gas infrastructure and broader industrial economy. (Corrects to clarify guest's comments in headline.) (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Amazon Ring Unveils $249 Smart Lock With Dial to Restore Dead Battery
summary: Amazon.com Inc.’s Ring brand unveiled its first smart lock, with an innovative feature that addresses the dreaded scenario of arriving home to a dead battery.

title: Raymond James Analyst Sees Nvidia Shares at $515
summary: Simon Leopold, Raymond James equity analyst, sees shares Nvidia rising to $515. The stock is trading near a record high with SpaceX reportedly in talks to raise $40 billion to buy Nvidia chips. Leopold is on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: McKinsey's Kutcher Says AI Creates Jobs and Opportunity
summary: Eric Kutcher, McKinsey & Co. chair of North America, is very bullish on the US economy. He says there will be more jobs in 2035 then there are today. He says artificial intelligence is creating jobs and points out that software developers who help AI write code are in high demand. He appears on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Apollo Trades $35 Billion Private Credit in Push to Open Market
summary: Apollo Global Management has traded more than $35 billion since it began making markets in private credit, according to John Cortese, partner and co-head of corporate credit.

title: SpaceX in Talks to Borrow $40 Billion to Buy Nvidia Chips
summary: Elon Musk’s SpaceX is in talks with banks and investors to raise $40 billion to buy chips from Nvidia Corp., people familiar with the matter said, in what would be among the biggest-ever debt financings for the AI buildout.

title: SpaceX Seeks To Join AI Borrowing Bonanza
summary:
SpaceX is joining the AI borrowing bonanza — seeking $40 billion to secure Nvidia chips.

Peter Elstrom explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: CoreWeave Tees Up First India Data Centers With AdaniConneX Deal
summary: AI cloud-computing provider CoreWeave Inc. is continuing an expansion in Asia with its first data centers in India, part of a venture involving conglomerate Adani Group.

title: Study: Claude, ChatGPT, AI Bots Offer Different Shopping Prices Based on Wealth
summary: Research on how Claude and ChatGPT act as shopping assistants could lead to more regulation calls.

title: AI Bots Swarm the Fed’s FRED Data Site as Jamie Dimon Warns of Security Risks
summary: AI agents seeking government data are introducing new vulnerabilities

title: ChatGPT for Teens Is Not Safe for Kids, Common Sense Media Report Says
summary: OpenAI’s ChatGPT for Teens — which the company rolled out in August as the default way for kids ages 13 to 17 use its popular chatbot — is too risky for children, according to a new report from Common Sense Media.
